name: Navan
summary: Business travel and expense management in one. Book trips, automate expense reports and control spend with real-time visibility.
best_for: companies of up to 300 employees that want self-serve travel booking with built-in policy control, free on Navan Business, and optionally unified expense management on top
skip_if: your travel volume is a few trips a year (any booking site does), or you need expense-only tooling without the travel layer
honest_knock: 'Free' is real but has a mechanism: Navan earns commission on bookings made through its inventory, so the platform's incentive is that your travel flows through Navan, and pricing on specific routes/hotels deserves an occasional spot-check against direct booking. The free Business plan stops at 300 employees and lists corporate negotiated rates as an Enterprise feature; expense management is free for 5 users and $15 per user per month after that.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per user a month from user 6
pricing.notes: (read 24 September 2026 on navan.com/pricing) Navan Business is free for companies of up to 300 employees, with no limit on trips, and Navan Expense is free for the first 5 monthly expensing users and then $15 per user per month. Above 300 employees the plan is Navan Enterprise, priced by quote. An expensing user is anyone who submits a transaction in the month, so the expense bill follows who actually files, not headcount. The travel side is free because it is funded by travel-supplier commissions, which makes the question not what it costs but what it steers; note that corporate negotiated rates sit in the Enterprise column of the plan table, not the Business one. Our July and August 2026 readings found no amount on this URL and put the free expense threshold at 15 users; the page now says 5, and this text follows the page.
